facts.text: Arcadia University began as Beaver Female Seminary in 1853, founded by the Methodist Episcopal Church to give young women a liberal arts education.
In 1872 the seminary gained collegiate status and became Beaver College and Musical Institute, expanding beyond women's arts to a full liberal arts college.
Grey Towers Castle, built in 1898, now serves as Arcadia University’s main administration building and is a National Historic Landmark.
Arcadia ranks first in the United States for undergraduate study abroad participation, according to the 2025 Open Doors Report.
The university’s origins trace back to a women’s seminary in Beaver, Pennsylvania, founded by educators Sylvania Jones and Juliet A.
The land where Arcadia sits was originally inhabited by the Lenape people, and the university acknowledges their stewardship in its land‑acknowledgement statement.
